chunks.text:
## Recent Database and Forensics Academic Work
During my current semester at UMT Sialkot, I have tackled several complex database and security projects. In October 2026, I developed a comprehensive database proposal for the Islamabad Diagnostic Center, which included mapping out a 7-table Entity-Relationship (ER) diagram. Following that, in November 2026, I completed an Advanced Database Management Systems lab project where I implemented a hospital Role-Based Access Control (HospitalRBAC_DB) system directly in SQL Server.

## Global Ambitions: Europe and Japan
I am actively planning my post-graduation trajectory. I am researching European Master's degree programs in Computer Science and software engineering. My goal is to study in Europe and secure a Werkstudent (working student) opportunity to gain international industry experience.

Simultaneously, I am exploring the technology sector in Japan. I am independently studying the Japanese language to prepare for future career opportunities there. I am specifically looking at pathways in cybersecurity, DevOps, and cloud engineering for a potential relocation to Japan once my foundational studies are complete.

## AI Automation and Freelance Development
As a freelance software developer and AI automation specialist on Fiverr, I focus on building intelligent, scalable systems. My core offerings revolve around creating advanced workflows using LangChain, LangGraph, n8n, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines. I also have a strong interest in Agentic AI frameworks, actively exploring Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (FastMCP) for autonomous multi-agent task execution.

*   **Mobile Application Development (React Native):** I am building two major mobile apps using React Native, Expo Router, and TypeScript. The first is **Kollab**, a peer-to-peer student networking and project collaboration app that integrates Supabase, PostgreSQL RLS, and Stripe for payments. *   **Maxing Enterprises:** For this leather apparel exporter, I created a complete technical B2B web blueprint, an SEO strategy, and produced showcase videos.

chunks.title: Project Retrospective: The FocusSpace Pivot
chunks.text:
## Initial Concept: A Minimalist Student Dashboard
During my Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) coursework at UMT Sialkot, my usual team of classmates and I embarked on a project we called FocusSpace. The original vision was to build a highly minimalist student dashboard. We wanted to apply core HCI principles to reduce cognitive load, strictly limiting the number of UI elements on the screen to help students track their academic progress without feeling overwhelmed. We spent weeks mapping out user flows, designing wireframes, and ensuring the color palette and typography met accessibility standards.

## The 11th-Hour Pivot
Just one day before our final academic presentation, we realized the minimalist dashboard, while visually pleasing, lacked the technical depth required to truly stand out. In a massive, sudden shift, we pivoted the entire architecture. We abandoned the basic student dashboard concept and transformed FocusSpace into an AI-assisted website UI checker.

## The Challenge and Execution
This was not necessarily the hardest raw coding I have ever done, but it was incredibly challenging due to the intense thought process required to execute a pivot that late in the game. We had to figure out how to integrate an AI layer that could actively analyze a given web interface and provide real-time heuristic feedback based on the exact HCI principles we had been studying.

We mapped specific UI heuristics—like visibility of system status, error prevention, and aesthetic minimalism—into actionable prompts for the AI. The system would then parse UI elements and flag areas where a website violated these rules. The intense time crunch meant we had no room for error. We pulled a late-night session (fueled by Mr. Foodie burgers) to stitch the frontend interface to the backend logic.

chunks.title: My Opinions, Hobbies, and Tastes
chunks.text:
## The Philosophy of Steam Profiles and Digital Aesthetics
When it comes to digital identity, I believe your Steam profile is a blank canvas. I spend a lot of time customizing digital Steam profiles, but I have a strong opinion here: I couldn't care less about crafted badges or game achievements. The true art lies in bespoke vector artwork, perfectly looped animated showcases, and tailored backgrounds. I use Adobe Illustrator for vector tracing and Photoshop for bringing AI-generated concepts to life.

Beyond static graphics, I genuinely enjoy the rhythm of video editing. Splicing together short-form digital video content—especially high-energy European football highlights—is one of my favorite creative outlets.

## Gaming Setup and Preferences
I am a late-night gamer at heart. My primary competitive arenas are Counter-Strike 2 and Team Fortress 2. I have a very specific take on optimal gaming performance: visual clarity and framerate trump graphical fidelity every time. That is why I strictly play CS2 on a 4:3 stretched resolution at 1440x1080. When paired with a 200 Hz display, the absolute smoothness gives a distinct mechanical advantage. I also recently added EA Sports FC 26 to my rotation to scratch the football itch virtually.

## Entertainment: Anime, Music, and Football
My taste in media is pretty focused. For anime, I appreciate the absolute classics and modern heavy hitters. *Great Teacher Onizuka* is top-tier because Eikichi Onizuka's character dynamic is unmatched, and I closely follow *Jujutsu Kaisen*, specifically for the raw intensity of Ryomen Sukuna.

chunks.title: Personal FAQ
chunks.text:
**Q: What is your primary development setup?**
A: I run a Windows desktop setup with an AMD Ryzen 5 5600 processor, an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 GPU, and 16 GB of RAM. I do most of my coding in Visual Studio Code using local Python virtual environments.

**Q: How do you handle AI models locally?**
A: I keep my models on a dedicated secondary drive (`D:\LLM_Models`). I deploy local open-source models, specifically Gemma 4, using LM Studio and Ollama connected via local OpenAI-compatible REST API endpoints.

**Q: What games do you play competitively?**
A: I mostly play tactical first-person shooters on PC, specifically Team Fortress 2 and Counter-Strike 2.

**Q: What are your CS2 settings?**
A: I play CS2 on a 4:3 stretched resolution at 1440x1080. It helps maximize visual clarity and smoothness on my 200 Hz display.

**Q: What kind of anime do you watch?**
A: I'm a big fan of Great Teacher Onizuka (Eikichi Onizuka is a classic) and Jujutsu Kaisen, especially the dynamic with Ryomen Sukuna.

**Q: What are your post-graduation plans?**
A: I am currently researching European Master's degree programs in Computer Science and looking into Werkstudent opportunities. I'm also independently studying Japanese and exploring pathways in cybersecurity, DevOps, and cloud engineering for a potential relocation to Japan.

**Q: What kind of music do you listen to?**
A: I mostly listen to Punjabi music. Karan Aujla is definitely one of my favorite artists right now.

A: I mainly use Payoneer, but honestly, they tax a lot and their deduction fees are really high.

**Q: What was the highlight of your trip to the Lahore Fort (Shahi Qila)?**
A: The trip itself was good, but our group didn't enter the fortress on time because we completely mismanaged our schedule and spent way too long on VR gaming beforehand. Seeing all the other students enjoying the fortress while we missed out definitely gave me a little pain!

**Q: What is your "hot take" regarding AI and the future of software engineering?**
A: My thought is that the things we learn become outdated incredibly fast, so we need to stay updated with tech as much as possible. Also, I think there is going to be a really good business for people creating professional AI agents that end up taking other people's jobs XD
